svg.title: Cepheid distance ladder and calibration
svg.desc: Four rungs, distance increasing upward. Kepler gives relative orbits in astronomical units. Transit timings, together with Earth's radius, give the astronomical unit as a length. Parallax uses that length as a baseline and reaches nearby stars, including nearby Cepheids. Leavitt's common-distance sample fixes the slope of the period-luminosity relation; the zero point is pinned later by parallax and other rungs. The plot is a sketch of a sliding zero point, not Leavitt's twenty-five stars. Type Ia supernovae are marked only as the next rung.
svg.text: The slope is not yet a distance
Distance grows upward. The plot is a sketch of the idea. Leavitt's twenty-five stars are on the Harvard page.
